clue.text: A quiet Italian river location may be suitable

parts.note: taken as written
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
the Po is Italy's longest river
a site is a location

explanation.surface: Someone scouting a quiet riverside spot in Italy thinks it might be just right.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means apt or well-chosen, a close synonym of suitable.

clue.text: Navy member, a US lawyer

parts.note: an arm is a limb, a member of the body
taken as written
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: A sailor in the navy turns out to be an American attorney.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' is a limb here, not someone belonging to the navy.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, a navy in the sense of a nation's ships.

clue.text: Friendly foreign correspondent?

parts.note: surface reading: a sociable journalist reporting from abroad
setter's reading: a friend overseas you exchange letters with

explanation.walkthrough: A foreign correspondent is normally a newspaper reporter abroad; here it is anyone who writes letters from another country.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen pal is a friend, often abroad, with whom one keeps up a letter-writing relationship.

clue.text: Naval base was focal point, primarily in the wars

indicators.note: someone in the wars is battered and knocked about, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the initial letter is used

parts.note: the word's first letter

explanation.surface: A naval base was the centre of operations in wartime.
explanation.walkthrough: Scapa Flow, in Orkney, was the Royal Navy's main anchorage in both World Wars, so the surface is literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Scapa Flow is the sheltered Orkney anchorage that served as Britain's chief fleet base.

clue.text: Those people getting to a super new play

parts.note: them refers to those people

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are put together differently

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Some people are off to see a wonderful new play.
explanation.walkthrough: Agatha Christie's whodunnit has run in London's West End since 1952, the world's longest-running play.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mousetrap is a famous stage play, Agatha Christie's murder mystery.

clue.text: A wife, after lively dances, brings out puzzle

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the dances in the reading order

parts.note: jigs are lively folk dances
taken as written
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: After an evening of energetic dancing, a wife gets out a puzzle to wind down.
explanation.definitionFit: A jigsaw is a picture-assembly puzzle of interlocking cut pieces.

clue.text: Playwright at home having caught disease

indicators.note: having caught something means holding it within

parts.note: in means at home
BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A dramatist falls ill while staying at home.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Director crosses off last character in scene

indicators.note: off means gone wrong or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the last character of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the word's final letter

explanation.surface: A film director strikes out the final line of a scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American film director of Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: Battle song

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Napoleon's final defeat, in 1815

explanation.walkthrough: Read together the words suggest a battle hymn; they are two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian village gave its name to Wellington's victory over Napoleon, and ABBA used it as a song title.

clue.text: A tiger, for example, better groomed by mother

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
neater means tidier, better groomed

explanation.surface: A child compares a pet tiger's grooming with mother's handiwork.
explanation.walkthrough: The mother piece comes first in the answer though last in the clue; 'by' just sets the two side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger that has killed people is an example of a man-eating animal.

clue.text: Armed guard in foreign sector

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange and unfamiliar, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Soldiers are posted to protect someone in an overseas zone.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a protective detachment, often armed, accompanying a person or convoy.

clue.text: Encourages Arnold, perhaps, to get something for breakfast?

parts.note: to egg someone on is to urge them
Benedict Arnold was the American Revolutionary general turned traitor; 'perhaps' marks him as one example of a Benedict

explanation.surface: Someone urges a friend called Arnold to fetch something for breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: Arnold looks like a first name but is the surname of Benedict Arnold, so here it stands for his given name.
explanation.definitionFit: This brunch dish is poached eggs and ham on an English muffin with hollandaise; the question mark flags its vagueness.

clue.text: Small drop to drink before opening of Anouilh play

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: the opening of a name is its very first letter

parts.note: the surname of the French dramatist

explanation.surface: A theatregoer has a quick whisky before an Anouilh play begins.
explanation.walkthrough: Jean Anouilh was a French playwright, which makes 'play' read as part of the scene rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play for the stage, or theatrical works generally.

clue.text: Arranger ran orgies in resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort again, putting things into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A party planner threw wild parties at a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' reads as a holiday place but works as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who arranges events or things is their organiser.

clue.text: Everything's ready — Sally nervously checks zip

indicators.note: a nervous person fidgets, so these letters jitter into a new order

parts.note: the name taken as anagram fodder
to stem is to check or stop a flow
zip and go both mean energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Before a big moment, Sally anxiously makes sure her zip is done up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'checks zip' looks like a nervous last look at clothing; checks is a verb meaning stems and zip is a noun meaning energy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a launch-control idiom announcing that every component is prepared.

clue.text: Expand on complex

definitions.meaning: first meaning, a verb: add more detail to
second meaning, an adjective: intricate, detailed

explanation.walkthrough: The verb and adjective are spelt alike but pronounced differently.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to develop in detail; as an adjective it means intricate and involved.

clue.text: Shiny silver paper in the street?

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
discarded wrappers and paper on the pavement; the question mark marks it as an example

explanation.surface: Silver wrapping paper glints in the gutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means glittering, sparkling with light, a poetic synonym of shiny.

clue.text: Ring found over in a river in Australian city

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, England and Scotland

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the word is read the other way

parts.note: to ring is to dial a telephone number

explanation.surface: A ring is recovered from a river near an Australian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like jewellery but is the verb, to phone.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the capital of South Australia.

clue.text: Fail utterly in warehouse to get articles placed round piano

parts.note: a godown is a warehouse in South and East Asia

indicators.note: things placed round something enclose it on both sides

parts.note: the definite and indefinite articles
p is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: Someone in a storehouse is told to arrange goods around a piano.
explanation.walkthrough: GODOWN is an Anglo-Indian word for warehouse, worth knowing for crosswords. The phrase is British slang, the pan being a toilet bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: To go down the pan is slang for being ruined or wasted completely, like something flushed away.

clue.text: Declare one's commitment to a small female company

parts.note: taken as written
small asks for the abbreviation, F for female
a firm is a business company

explanation.surface: A woman pledges loyalty to a modest firm.
explanation.definitionFit: To affirm something is to state support for it publicly, as one affirms a belief or an oath.

clue.text: Earnest request made by pair over New Year

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece over another means it sits above, coming first

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for pair

indicators.note: new signals a fresh arrangement of the letters that follow

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A couple make a heartfelt wish at New Year.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer can be any earnest plea or entreaty, not only one addressed to God.

clue.text: Hostile military command makes one uncomfortable

parts.note: ill as in ill will, unfriendly
'At ease!' is the order that lets soldiers relax

explanation.surface: An aggressive army order leaves a soldier feeling uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ill at ease is an idiom for feeling awkward or uncomfortable.

clue.text: Story about bishop and food

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a tale is a story
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A tale about a bishop and what he ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Table' for food is the sense in 'she keeps a good table'.
explanation.definitionFit: Table can mean the meals provided, as in a household's fare or the quality of its cooking.

clue.text: Cold leaving chest tender

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a coffer is a strongbox or chest
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A cold leaves someone's chest feeling sore.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests illness and a sore chest; tender is a verb meaning to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: To tender something, such as a resignation or bid, is to present or put it forward.

clue.text: Attempt to secure one pound for a hat

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, here by enclosing it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Roman numeral one
lb, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound in weight

explanation.surface: Someone tries to buy a hat for a single pound.
explanation.definitionFit: A trilby is a soft felt hat with an indented crown and narrow brim.

clue.text: Amusement caused by it during Spring term at Oxford

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls inside it

parts.note: Hilary is the name of the January to March term at Oxford
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something that happened in the spring term at Oxford caused much laughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford University names its three terms Michaelmas, Hilary and Trinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarity is loud merriment or great amusement.

clue.text: Hand-rolled cigarette in jacket

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a cannabis cigarette, slang
second meaning: a thick double-breasted sailor's jacket

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a roll-up tucked in a jacket pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a cannabis joint and also names a heavy naval-style jacket.

clue.text: Ship carrying right flag

indicators.note: a vessel carrying cargo holds it inside

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A vessel flies the correct flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A streamer is a long narrow pennant or ribbon-like flag.
